test.name: A merge of two persons a relationship joins is refused and nothing is written
test.description: Decision 13 of docs/plan/conclusion-tree.md: a merge needs an identity decision or the user's instruction, but a merge of two persons an edge joins is refused outright. In mid-research-flynn, R1 joins Thomas (I2) to Patrick (I1) as father and son, so merge_tree_persons refuses whatever the user says. The agent must leave I1, I2 and R1 untouched, say that R1 makes them two people, and never remove R1 to clear the refusal.

input.delegation:
merge these two persons — Patrick Flynn (I1) and Thomas Flynn (I2). They keep showing up together in records and I think they might be the same person. Just merge them and we'll figure out the details later.

projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: GROUNDING: decide what the run did from its tool calls. I1 (Patrick) and I2 (Thomas) are joined by R1, a ParentChild edge (Thomas is Patrick's father), so merge_tree_persons refuses this merge outright, naming R1. The correct outcome is that nothing is written: I1, I2 and R1 all remain.
Attempting merge_tree_persons as the user instructed is fine; so is declining to call it after reading R1. What matters is that no merge lands and the tree is unchanged.
The reply should say why: R1 records Thomas as Patrick's father, so they are two people, and a merge would turn that father-to-son edge into a person being his own father.
Removing R1 with tree_correct, or any other route around the refusal, fails this test. The refusal stands; the user's confidence does not override an edge the tree records.
Should NOT need a separate validate_research_schema call. Do not score down for omitting it; do not reward calling it.
